grammar_focus: KS37 表示将来的三种时态(将来进行时 will be doing、将来完成时 will have done、将来完成进行时 will have been doing)(教材 L61 Key structures)主考;时间/条件状语从句用一般现在/现在完成表将来(by the time you read this、the moment he has arrived)+ SD cost/price/value 名词与动词辨析(辅考)
scene: 哈勃望远镜于1990年4月20日由国家航空航天局发射升空,耗资10多亿美元。从最开始哈勃望远镜就有问题:它传送给我们的图像很令人失望,因为它的主镜子有误差。国家航空航天局准备纠正这一错误,为此不久将把4名宇航员送入太空修复望远镜。“奋进”号航天飞机将把宇航员送上哈勃。“奋进”号上的一只机器手将抓住望远镜并托住它,同时宇航员进行必要的修复工作。当然,哈勃位于地球大气层之外,因此它很快就会给我们传送来我们所见到过的、有关行星和遥远星系的最清晰的照片。哈勃将告诉我们许多有关宇宙的年龄和大小的事情。等到你读到这篇文章时,敏锐的哈勃望远镜已经为我们送来了成千上万张精彩的照片。

grammar_card.title: 表示将来的三种时态
grammar_card.intro: KS37 三种将来时态:①将来进行时 will be + 现在分词——表示将来某时正在进行的动作(I will be writing letters all day tomorrow);②将来完成时 will have + 过去分词——表示到将来某时已经完成的动作(Soon the astronauts will have repaired it);③将来完成进行时 will have been + 现在分词——表示到将来某时为止一直持续的动作(By Friday they will have been working on it for seven days)。

rows: I will be writing letters all day tomorrow.
Soon the astronauts will have repaired the telescope.
By Friday, they will have been working on it for seven days.
He will have arrived by this time tomorrow.

specialRules.rule: 在 by the time/the moment/as soon as 等引导的时间、条件状语从句中,用一般现在时或现在完成时表示将来,主句用将来时:By the time you read this, the Hubble will have sent us pictures;The moment he has arrived, I will let you know。

SD 易混词 cost/price/value:①作名词——cost 成本/造价(at a cost of),price 价钱(ask the price),value 价值(sentimental value);②作动词——cost 花费多少钱(What does it cost?),price 给…定价/问价(price the goods),value 重视/珍视(I value your advice)。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What is the special importance of a telescope in space?
options: Being above the atmosphere, it sends the clearest pictures of stars and distant galaxies
It is cheaper to build than one on earth
It can be repaired only by astronauts
It can travel to other galaxies

passage: The Hubble telescope was launched into space by NASA on April 20, 1990 at a cost of over a billion dollars. Right from the start there was trouble with the Hubble. The pictures it sent us were very disappointing because its main mirror was faulty! NASA is now going to put the telescope right, so it will soon be sending up four astronauts to repair it. The shuttle Endeavour will be taking the astronauts to the Hubble. A robot-arm from the Endeavour will grab the telescope and hold it while the astronauts make the necessary repairs. Of course, the Hubble is above the earth's atmosphere, so it will soon be sending us the clearest pictures of the stars and distant galaxies that we have ever seen. The Hubble will tell us a great deal about the age and size of the universe. By the time you read this, the Hubble's eagle eye will have sent us thousands and thousands of wonderful pictures.
